_comment: Recorded SUT baselines — measurements the repository can provenance, migrated from prose (#280). A batch is recorded history: it is not, by being here or by being the newest, the current or comparable baseline of its cases; a case measured in two batches has two entries and neither wins. `plugin` is an exact version or null with `plugin_range`; `date` is an exact run date or null with `date_range` (a sweep's span, not each case's run date). A result carries counts (`valid`, `passed`) or, where the record never wrote them down, its own words under `reported`. `superseded` names why a batch or a result no longer describes the case as it stands. tools/ledger.py renders evals/README.md's block from this file; a new baseline is a new batch here, then the tool. An instrument-only case (F6: its driver writes a curve, and the runner keeps it out of every pass count) is always `reported`, never counted. Every batch dated before 2026-11-14 is superseded by #293's corpus repair; the first post-repair sweep is the first batch that is not.
